correctness.rationale: The displayed cubic is geometrically smooth: at X=0 vanishing of the gradient gives the zero triple, and at X=1 it requires Z^3=4 and Z^3=3 simultaneously. An independent exact enumeration normalized the first nonzero coordinate to 1 and compared gradients up to nonzero scalar: 57 ambient points, 12 curve points, and exactly the 12 stated lines, with incidence histogram {1:36,2:9,3:9,5:3}. An algebraic replay of the affine locus uses (x,y)→(hx,h²y) for h³=1; x=1 and x=3 represent the nonzero cosets, giving y=5 and y∈{1,5}, respectively. The three orbit representatives have tangents X−Z, Y−Z, X−2Y, and the three axis points supply the coordinate tangents. Nonzero coordinate cubes take just two values, hence always give a covered pair; vanishing coordinates are covered directly. In the smooth conic case eight tangents have no triple concurrence by duality, so cover 36 points; singular quadratic forms have at most two component lines as tangents at smooth rational points, covering at most 15. A line covers eight. Frozen RESULT.md §§1–3 and verify.py give the proof and a finite replay path, respectively. The uploaded script was inspected, not run; the finite replay does not certify geometric smoothness or exhaustion over other fields.
